overall: The AG found the Arlington Human Rights Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the April 10 notice topic was sufficiently specific, and no rule requires handing out documents at meetings. The AG reminded the Commission about the less specific April 1 notice, which was not formally reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 10 notice topic on the Hingham statement (under a Gaza humanitarian crisis heading) lacked sufficient specificity.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that the topic as listed on the notice here was sufficient to reasonably advise the public of the issue to be discussed at the meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the April 1 notice topic on the tabled Hingham co-sign motion was noted as less specific than the April 10 notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the sufficiency of the April 1 meeting notice was not raised in the complaint, we do not formally review or find a violation of the Open Meeting Law regarding the April 1 notice; however, we note the contrast between the specificity of the two notices and remind the Commission of its obligations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to provide a copy of the Hingham statement under review at the April 10 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that the public body affirmatively provide copies of documents to persons in attendance at a meeting.
